why: I checked every command in both briefs against the repository. The files they name, src/config.js, test/config.test.js, src/app.js and README.md, are all tracked. `npm test` maps to `node --test`, which picks up test/config.test.js. The temp-file check `d=$(mktemp -d) && printf '{port: 9000' > "$d/config.json" && node --input-type=module -e "..." "$d/config.json"; echo "exit=$?"` has valid shell syntax. Its double-quoted JavaScript contains no `$` or backticks, so the shell won't expand anything inside it. With `-e`, `process.argv[1]` is the first extra argument, so it gets the temp file path. The relative `./src/config.js` import resolves from the repository root, where both briefs run their commands. The missing-file command and `npm test; echo "exit=$?"` are valid too. One thing I couldn't confirm: whether config.js is an ES module, since package.json's "type" field isn't shown. Node can import it either way, so the commands should run as written.
